title: Fail-closed reproducibility for finite quantum sequential growth: exact controls, independent replay, and resource boundaries

description: We report a fail-closed reproducibility framework for finite quantum sequential-growth calculations. The framework separates candidate evidence from controls, binds claims to versioned machine-readable artifacts, requires independent replay before promotion, and records resource limits as open boundaries. Existing bounded artifacts include a five-seed small-n sampler regression, 40 deterministic sampler fixtures, eight four-dimensional Minkowski-control fixtures, and five synthetic supervisor modes. In a separate exact random-growth scaling review, primary and independent paths complete growth through cardinality 38 with identical digests; an attempted step from source size 38 detects at least 4,097 down-sets and fails closed at the declared cap of 4,096. This is a resource-limit observation, not an impossibility theorem. No candidate production evidence, continuum-limit result, or final-theory claim is made.

additional_descriptions.description: Scope and claim boundary. The upload reports bounded exact controls, deterministic ticket and replay contracts, digest-checked atomic promotion, synthetic wall-time/memory/disk supervisor fixtures, and an exact enumeration boundary. The 40 deterministic fixtures and the separate five-seed, 1,024-trajectory-per-seed regression are implementation checks, not production measurements. The uniform-control ideal-count recurrence is design-only and was not used to generate new production trajectories. The candidate's nonlocal link/diamond/precursor weight has no certified reduced-state factorisation in this project, so candidate production access is excluded. The work does not claim N=60 completion, production spectral dimension, a BDG ensemble, full 955/721 resolution, a complete finite occurrence-ON semantics lattice, solver impossibility, or closure of FINAL_THEORY_OPEN.

Authorship and AI assistance. The human author is responsible for all claims and release decisions. OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude assisted bounded implementation, artifact audit, verification, and prose drafting. AI systems are not authors or independent proof authorities.
